chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (the first Imam), peace be upon him: 'When a man takes a house and passes by it, does he complete his prayer or shorten it?' He said: 'Every house that you do not make your permanent residence is not considered a house for you, and you are not to complete your prayer in it.'
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence define a 'home' versus 'travel' for the purpose of shortening prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the criterion for 'residence' (watan) in the context of travel prayer, establishing that temporary lodging does not negate the traveler's status. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that qasr applies unless one intends to stay for a specific duration (typically ten days) or has a permanent home, ensuring ease for the traveler. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic law in accommodating the practical realities of movement and temporary habitation.
